description: Given two integer arrays inorder and postorder where inorder is the inorder traversal and postorder is the postorder traversal of a binary tree, construct and return the binary tree.
intuition: The last element of postorder is always the root. Find that root in the inorder array to determine which elements belong to the left vs. right subtree. Process postorder from right to left, building the right subtree before the left, since postorder visits right subtrees later.
approach: The last element of postorder is the root. Find it in inorder to split into left and right subtrees. Recursively build right subtree first (since postorder processes right before left when going backwards), then left subtree.
jsWalkthrough:
Input: inorder = [9,3,15,20,7], postorder = [9,15,7,20,3]

inorderMap = {9:0, 3:1, 15:2, 20:3, 7:4}, postIdx = 4

build(0, 4):
  rootVal = postorder[4] = 3, postIdx -> 3
  mid = inorderMap[3] = 1
  Build right subtree: build(2, 4)
    rootVal = postorder[3] = 20, postIdx -> 2
    mid = inorderMap[20] = 3
    Build right: build(4, 4)
      rootVal = postorder[2] = 7, postIdx -> 1
      mid = 4, build(5,4) -> null, build(4,3) -> null
      return node(7)
    Build left: build(2, 2)
      rootVal = postorder[1] = 15, postIdx -> 0
      mid = 2, both sides null
      return node(15)
    return node(20, left=15, right=7)
  Build left subtree: build(0, 0)
    rootVal = postorder[0] = 9, postIdx -> -1
    mid = 0, both sides null
    return node(9)
  return node(3, left=9, right=20)

Result tree: [3,9,20,null,null,15,7]
explanation:
1. Build a map from value to index in inorder for O(1) lookup.
2. Start from the last element of postorder (the root).
3. Find root in inorder to determine left and right subtree ranges.
4. Build right subtree first (postorder: left, right, root - so right is before root).
5. Then build left subtree. Decrement post_idx each time we create a node.
hints: The last element of postorder is always the root.
Use inorder to determine which elements go in the left vs right subtree.
Build right subtree before left when consuming postorder from the end.
